nodes.title: Store each selection as a set of ids
nodes.why: The top selection is a set of item ids in a signal, typed ReadonlySet so code cannot add to it in place; ids stay valid when moves shift item positions.
nodes.alternative: Keep a selected flag on each item, or store the indexes of the checked rows.
nodes.tradeoff: A separate set keeps items plain and lookups constant time, but it must be cleared when its items leave the list; flags on items would travel with them and need resetting instead.

nodes.title: Derive the arrow button state
nodes.why: The down arrow is enabled exactly when the top selection is not empty; the computed updates whenever toggleTop or moveDown sets a new set.
nodes.alternative: Keep canMoveDown as a boolean field and flip it in every toggle and move handler.
nodes.tradeoff: The computed cannot fall out of step with the selection, but it only notices new sets, which is why toggles copy the set instead of editing it.

nodes.title: Append moved items to the end of the other list
nodes.why: Moved items go after the existing bottom items in a new array, so Bottom keeps its order and its rows, and @for creates rows only for the arrivals.
nodes.alternative: Insert moved items at the top, or re-sort the destination by label after every move.
nodes.tradeoff: Appending follows the spec and leaves existing rows where they are; sorted insertion would read better in long lists but shifts rows the user was looking at.

nodes.title: Clear the source selection after a move
nodes.why: The moved ids no longer belong to Top, so the top selection becomes a new empty set, which also disables the down arrow; the bottom selection is left as it was.
nodes.alternative: Delete only the moved ids from the set, or carry the selection over so moved items arrive checked.
nodes.tradeoff: Every selected top item moves, so clearing the whole set is exact here; carrying the selection over would let users move items straight back but breaks the spec.

nodes.title: Copy the set on every toggle
nodes.why: toggled() builds a new Set before adding or deleting the id, so the selection signal receives a new reference and canMoveDown and canMoveUp recompute.
nodes.alternative: Call add or delete on the set the signal already holds.
nodes.tradeoff: Copying costs one new set per click, while in-place edits keep the reference: the signal never notifies and the arrow button stays disabled after the first check.

nodes.title: Split in list order, not click order
nodes.why: Filtering the source list keeps its order, so items checked as Gamma then Alpha still arrive as Alpha, Gamma; the second filter keeps the remaining items in order too.
nodes.alternative: Build moved by iterating the selection set, which follows the order the boxes were checked.
nodes.tradeoff: Two filter passes read each item twice, which only matters for very long lists; one loop that fills two arrays avoids it but takes more code to read.
